thread:
jordan: Heads-up — I discovered a public S3 object that contains an encrypted blob which looks like a Vault backup wrapped with our staging KMS key. Link: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-backups-staging/2026-03-21/backup.tar.gz :eyes:

maya: Ugh. Is it plaintext creds or just wrapped ciphertext?

jordan: Looks like ciphertext only, base64 blob inside tar. I haven’t tried decrypting. Object was public for ~6 hours according to S3 ACL history.

sam: Can you paste the object metadata (ETag, last-modified) and the KMS key alias you see in the envelope?

jordan: Metadata: ETag "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e", last-modified 2026-03-21T02:14:03Z. The blob references alias/aws/kms (staging-key-redwood).

otto: First triage: assume secret compromise until proven otherwise. Steps: 1) snapshot object and make copy, 2) check CloudTrail/CloudWatch for KMS Decrypt calls, 3) rotate affected keys/tokens. I can take 1 and 2.

jordan: Copy saved to internal bucket s3://redwood-security-evidence/4412349999/backup.tar.gz

security-bot: Alert created: INCIDENT-2026-03-21-ksg. Ticket #INC-2319. Notifying oncall.

oncall: Acknowledged. I’ll stand up the incident channel if we need an incident war room.

maya: Sam/otto — for Vault: which tokens could be in a backup? Unseal keys? Root token? Mount tokens? We need a list to rotate.

sam: Vault backup likely contains sealed data + wrapped tokens/leases. If this is a full snapshot, we must assume any unsealed secrets could be reconstructed if someone can unwrap KMS + transit. Immediate actions: revoke any long-lived staging service tokens, rotate transit key, and rotate KMS wrapping key (rekey).

eli: Question — can we rotate KMS alias for staging immediately without breaking running staging services? We need a maintenance window.

otto: We can create a new staging key and set the alias to point to it. Rewrap old ciphertext where necessary. We should not delete old key until we confirm all rewraps succeed.

jordan: I started a quick hunt: grep inside the tar shows files under vault-backups/ that look like: vault_snapshot_2026-03-21.snap (binary) and a vault-transit-wrapped blob file.

maya: Who owns the S3 ACL that made it public? Any partner uploads?

jordan: Looks like a CI job (team: integrations) pushed it. The job used a partner-provided artifact step. I pinged @integrations lead but no answer yet.

sam: Action items (short):
- otto: fetch CloudTrail logs for KMS Decrypt, list principal ARNs in last 48h
- jordan: preserve object (done), capture ACLs, and snapshot tar contents (done)
- maya: prepare Vault revocation plan and list of tokens/roles to rotate
- eli: plan KMS key rotation + alias swap; advise on rewrap approach
- oncall: create incident channel and invite infra/product/security as needed

otto: Running CloudTrail query now. If we see any successful Decrypt by non-Redwood principals -> escalate to legal and partner-eng.

security-bot: CloudTrail query job queued: job-id ct-4412349999-1. Results in ~3m.

jordan: FYI snippet of the tar listing:
```
$ tar -tf backup.tar.gz
vault-backups/vault_snapshot_2026-03-21.snap
vault-backups/wrapped-kms-blob.b64
```

maya: Good. Assume possible sensitive exposures. Sam, start revoking staging service tokens that are long-lived. Prioritize CI runner service accounts and any integration service principals.

sam: On it. Revoked: staging-runner-token-03, staging-partner-svcacc-2. Also kicked CI pipelines that had keys. Will issue follow-up list in the incident channel.

otto: CloudTrail shows no successful Decrypt calls from external principals in the last 7 days. Only our staging bastion and the integrations CI role tried to call Decrypt at 02:15 UTC (last-modified time). I’ll paste full ARNs in the channel.

eli: Given that, we still need KMS rotation because the object was public. Proposed low-risk plan: create new CMK (staging-key-2026-03-21), update alias staging-key-redwood -> new CMK, update CI to use new key, then rewrap backup artifacts we care about. Notify partner to audit their upload pipeline.

maya: Also put an RBAC guard: block S3 PutObject public ACLs for integrations bucket. Add a bucket-policy deny for "aws:PutObjectAcl" when ACL == "public-read" for that bucket. I can file the PR for infra.

jordan: I filed a quick issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-4412 for the RBAC and bucket-policy change.

oncall: Created incident channel #inc-2319-secret-leak, invited listed folks.

sam: We should rotate Vault auto-unseal key bindings for staging too. If staging uses KMS for auto-unseal, swapping alias will break unseal if not coordinated. Eli: coordinate with Vault ops — we may need to rekey/unseal in maintenance window.

eli: Agree. Plan: schedule a 30m window midday UTC, create snapshot of current state, perform alias swap and restart unseal agent if needed, confirm services come back. We’ll do a canary host first.

maya: I’ll coordinate with integrations to block any further external uploads and require PR review for artifact steps. Also looping legal to draft partner notification.

jordan: Quick sanity check — no prod keys referenced, confirmed. This is staging-only per IAM cross-check.

otto: Good. I’ll keep monitoring CloudTrail and S3 access logs for any GETs to the public object.

security-bot: CloudTrail query done: no external decrypts found (job ct-4412349999-1).

jordan: I’ll reach out to integrations lead and partner-ops with the evidence bundle (s3 snapshot location) and request immediate ACL removal on their side.

sam: Post-actions: rotate staging transit key, rotate KMS alias, revoke long-lived tokens (done), update CI to use new key, enforce bucket policy, run a postmortem.

maya: I’ve drafted the postmortem skeleton and assigned owners. Will attach timelines after the KMS rotation.

eli: I created new CMK and staged alias swap. Will coordinate the 30m window on #inc-2319.

otto: After alias swap, we should rewrap any backups we still keep with new key and then delete public copies.

jordan: Confirmed partner removed public ACL and integrations put guard rails. I’m going to mark this thread as 'working' and we’ll update the incident channel for final closure.

sam: Thanks everyone. I’ll post the token rotation list in the incident channel.

jordan: Closing slack thread — see #inc-2319 for live status and final postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
